description: I-JSON acceptance boundary vectors (spec/canonicalization.md). `input_json` is the raw JSON text an implementation must feed to its own parser plus canonicalizer. `expect: accept` pins the canonical output; `expect: reject` requires the value to be refused, at parse time or at canonicalization time, whichever this lane reaches first. Both are conforming: what is normative is that the value never reaches a hash.

reasons.integer_out_of_range: A number whose canonical token is a plain integer literal (no '.', no 'e') with |n| > 2^53 - 1.
reasons.unpaired_surrogate: A string, or an object key, containing a surrogate code point that is not part of a well-formed pair.

vectors.name: duplicate-member-basic
vectors.note: RFC 7493 2.3: objects must not have members with duplicate names. Every mainstream parser silently keeps the last value, so two different byte sequences share one canonical form — a smuggling primitive. Refusal at parse time or at the canonicalization gate both conform.

vectors.name: duplicate-member-nested
vectors.note: The rule applies at every depth, not just the top-level object.

vectors.name: duplicate-member-escaped-name
vectors.note: Names compare AFTER escape processing: \u0061 is the same member name as a. A text-level duplicate detector that compares raw escape sequences misses this pair.
